messages.subject: Minimum number of locations
parts:
Hi Chris,

I am running home ranges in 'ctmm' for a set of ground squirrels.  The data were collected in 2003-2004, so they are VHF radiotelemetry data.  This means there are not very many locations for each squirrel.  I'm wondering about the minimum number of locations required to calculate a 'ctmm' home range.  When examining the variogram for an asymptote, if there are too few locations, you cannot really tell if it has an asymptote, correct?  Is there a "rule" that there should be a minimum number of locations to determine if a variogram has an asymptote?

Thanks for your help and any guidance you can provide on this issue.

Sharon

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Minimum number of locations
parts:
Hi Sharon,

There is a lot of information on the required amount of data in https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/2041-210X.13270

There isn't a minimum number of points per se (unless the data are IID), but more a minimum number of observed range crossings, which is also dependent on the estimator being used and the tolerance for bias. Often times with IID VHF data, people are surprised when I tell them that their 20 locations are worth more than a year of Mongolian gazelle data. Variograms can be hard to look at when there isn't much data, so you might try pooling individuals with the mean() function ( https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/reference/mean.variogram.html ).

Best,
Chris
